transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-04
Start time: 14:30 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Jamie (Redwood AE), Ravi (Redwood SE), Lena (Redwood Solutions), Maya (Silverline Head of ML), Ethan (CTO), Sophie (Infra), Oliver (Finance)

[00:00] Jamie Chen: hey everyone thanks for joining, can you hear me ok?
[00:04] Maya Lopez: yeah loud and clear, thanks.
[00:08] Jamie Chen: awesome quick agenda — wanna focus on cost per unit economics, how batching/caching changes the math, and what Dedicated vs Hosted vs Private looks like for a quick pilot. ravi will jump into some numbers.
[00:18] Ravi Patel: yeah hi all, i'll keep it high level then we can go deeper. quick question, maya — what's the main workload mix? is it low-latency request/response for trading signals or bulk offline summarization?
[00:29] Maya Lopez: main is low-latency inference for signals at market open and intra-day alerts, approx 120k requests a day but very spiky, plus a smaller set of nightly summarizations. Typical prompt length is 80-160 tokens in, and we see about 120-250 tokens out.
[00:45] Ethan Brooks: and our SLO is sub-200ms p95 for the trading latency path — if that grows we're in trouble.
[00:52] Sophie Chen: infra-wise we run k8s on GCP, have a VPC and strict egress rules, and we need SAML SSO + KMS for keys.
[00:59] Jamie Chen: got it, thanks. big picture: Hosted API is fastest to evaluate but per-token cost higher, Dedicated reserved capacity gives predictable unit economics and better tail latency for spiky traffic, and Private (VPC/on-prem) gives control for compliance but higher ops cost.
[01:15] Ravi Patel: jumping into the cost math — baseline hosted price for a 70B-ish open model in market is X cents per 1k prompt tokens and Y cents per 1k completion tokens — for redwood we present as total per-token unit; real numbers we shared in the deck but to illustrate, with current profile you'd pay roughly $0.03-$0.08 per 1k tokens on hosted depending on batching and model.
[01:36] Oliver Grant: sorry can you repeat that range?
[01:38] Ravi Patel: yeah, approx $0.03 to $0.08 per 1k tokens on hosted — big variance from batching and whether you're using quantized variants.
[01:46] Maya Lopez: that seems pretty broad. how much does batching actually shift that?
[01:50] Ravi Patel: batching is huge — with continuous batching and our runtime we can consolidate many short requests into a single GPU forward. for your profile, if you can allow 30-60ms queuing you might get a 2x-4x effective token throughput improvement, which directly cuts per-token cost. if you need the <200ms p95 we need to simulate queueing tradeoffs.
[02:08] Ethan Brooks: excuse me quick — you mentioned KV cache and prefix caching earlier in the deck, how does that affect cost?
[02:12] Ravi Patel: yeah good Q. prefix / kv cache reduces compute by reusing cached past keys for repeated contexts. for stateful convo or repeated prompt prefixes you can see 20-60% token compute savings depending on cache hit rate. for stateless single-shot calls less impact. Maya, you said prompts are often similar at market open?
[02:29] Maya Lopez: yeah we have a standard system prompt + market snapshot that changes but parts are identical across calls. we also use some small context windows we keep across requests for a given symbol.
[02:37] Ravi Patel: so you should get decent cache hit rates for the early tokens — that reduces cost and latency. also quantization — running 4-bit or int8 variants reduces throughput per GPU but increases batch density so unit cost often drops. small accuracy tradeoffs to test.
[02:54] Sophie Chen: on Dedicated — how do reserved capacity pricing and burst capacity numbers look? our traffic is spiky so we need headroom two times average at open.
[03:02] Jamie Chen: Dedicated is modelled as a monthly reserved capacity. you pay for a set of GPU capacity (e.g., N A100/RTX or equivalent instances) and get predictable throughput. we typically size for p95 and then allow short burst pools. price per token is lower because you amortize instance cost across more tokens. for a short pilot we can do a time-limited reservation and include a burst pool for the open window.
[03:21] Oliver Grant: do you have a sample calculation? if we target $15k/month budget what does that get us?
[03:25] Ravi Patel: quick napkin — $15k/mo on Dedicated could cover a small cluster (2-4 GPUs depending on hardware), which for optimized model + batching might do ~2M-6M tokens/day at reasonable latency. exact depends on sequence length and model. we sent a sizing example in the deck; i'll push a tailored one after we get your sample traffic.
[03:44] Maya Lopez: what about Private? we need VPC and KMS, and SOC2 compliance — is that just an add-on?
[03:50] Jamie Chen: Redwood Private gives you customer-managed network and KMS/HSM integration; there's an enterprise licensing fee plus infra ops. SOC2 and audit logs are supported and we can provide SOC2 attestation and the security pack. latency and per-token economics look similar to Dedicated if you manage equivalent hardware, but ops overhead for you will be higher.
[04:08] Ethan Brooks: any chance to do an A/B of hosted vs dedicated for a week-like pilot? we want to see real tail latency and cost numbers on our traffic.
[04:14] Ravi Patel: absolutely — common approach: run hosted for ingest + shadow mode to capture traffic while we run a Dedicated sizing estimate, then run a short dedicated pilot for the spike window. we can also do a benchmark run if you give sample traffic and a small dataset.
[04:27] Sophie Chen: our security checklist includes SAML SSO, KMS, CORS lock-down, and audit trails — do you have those ready?
[04:34] Jamie Chen: yes we support SSO/SAML, KMS integrations, RBAC, and audit logs. we'll attach the security docs in the follow-up and our SE will coordinate any pen-test or SOC2-specific artifacts.
[04:45] Maya Lopez: on accuracy — you mentioned quantization tradeoffs. we'd need to validate quality on our eval prompts. how do you recommend we run that?
[04:52] Ravi Patel: simplest is run a small eval set through both float32 and quantized variants and compare metrics you care about (F1/accuracy or human eval). we can help run those in the pilot; our Optimize tooling flags regressions and suggests quantization profiles.
[05:06] Oliver Grant: circling back to cost — you said batching might add latency. what's a realistic queuing tolerance for our 200ms p95?
[05:13] Ravi Patel: if you need strict <200ms p95 you'll likely be in a lower batching regime — improvements more modest maybe 1.2x-2x. if you can tolerate 300-400ms p95 you can push for 3x-4x efficiency. it's a tradeoff between user experience and cost.
[05:27] Maya Lopez: tradeoffs here make sense. our ops team could accept up to 300ms p95 if the signal quality and cost improvement are good.
[05:35] Jamie Chen: noted. also worth calling out network egress and tokenization inefficiencies — trimming prompts, doing client-side tokenization batching, or local prefix expansion can reduce billed tokens.
[05:47] Ethan Brooks: what's Redwood's outage/fallback strategy if Dedicated capacity is saturated?
[05:52] Ravi Patel: smart routing — we can route to a hosted fallback or a lower-cost smaller model for non-critical traffic. rollouts support canary and automatic fallback. we also have autoscaling policies for Dedicated with burst capacity.
[06:05] Sophie Chen: any gotchas for k8s integration if we go Private on GCP?
[06:09] Ravi Patel: the Private package has a control plane and customer-managed compute; you can run inference nodes in your k8s cluster or on dedicated hardware. networking and egress rules are supported but we'll need to scope exact firewall rules.
[06:19] Jamie Chen: okay let's do a recap of immediate asks — maya share sample traffic and prompts; jamie sends pricing sheet and batching guide; ravi will size Dedicated pilot and propose hardware; we'll schedule pilot kickoff next week.
[06:32] Maya Lopez: sounds good. one last question — do you publish latency breakdowns by token vs model variant?
[06:37] Ravi Patel: yes our console shows per-token compute, queueing, and network for routes and models; we'll give you a sample dashboard screenshot.
[06:45] Oliver Grant: thanks all, we'll look at the numbers and get the sample files over.
[06:50] Jamie Chen: great thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the docs and a calendar invite for the pilot planning.
[06:55] call ends
